abstract.para: &kdump; usually fails at one of three points: the crash kernel memory reservation is insufficient, the capture kernel fails to boot or save the dump, or the dump cannot be written to its destination. Use the checks below to narrow down which stage is failing.

section.title: Crash kernel memory reservation is insufficient
section.para: If a crash produces error messages about low memory, or the Out Of Memory (OOM) killer being invoked inside the capture kernel, the reserved crash kernel memory is too small for this system. This can happen even after following , since the right amount depends on the actual workload running at the time of the crash.

step.para: Check the currently reserved amount from the kernel command line:
Add up every crashkernel= value shown (a plain value, or separate ,low/,high values) to get the current total reservation in MiB.
Edit /etc/sysconfig/kdump and roughly double KDUMP_CRASHKERNEL from the current total:
Reboot to apply the new reservation, then try to reproduce the crash again. See .
Repeat with smaller increases until the dump completes reliably. A note taken between the last failing and the last working size narrows down a reasonable final value faster than repeatedly doubling.

varlistentry.term: The screen stays blank during the capture kernel boot

listitem.para: Configure a serial console so the capture kernel's boot messages are captured somewhere you can read them. A blank local console gives you nothing to debug from. Once you have output, increase logging by setting KDUMP_VERBOSE="11" in /etc/sysconfig/kdump. This removes the quiet kernel option from the capture kernel's command line and runs both the dump-saving step and makedumpfile with debugging output enabled.

varlistentry.term: makedumpfile or network configuration errors during capture

listitem.para: Set KDUMP_CONTINUE_ON_ERROR="false" or KDUMP_IMMEDIATE_REBOOT="false". Instead of rebooting automatically, this drops you into an interactive shell inside the capture environment when an error occurs, or once makedumpfile finishes, so you can inspect the problem directly.

varlistentry.term: Dracut errors during the capture kernel boot

listitem.para: Add dracut's own debugging options to KDUMP_COMMANDLINE_APPEND in /etc/sysconfig/kdump, for example, KDUMP_COMMANDLINE_APPEND="rd.debug".
